principles: Refuse true duplicates explicitly rather than silently piling on verdicts.
Do not regress the first legitimate quorum submission.
Key the guard on observable state (runId + materialDigest), not wall-clock or call count.
Match the handler's existing refusal style and write nothing on refusal.
drivers: Prevent duplicate verdicts under an already-populated runId.
Still allow a fresh quorum after a genuine material change + re-review.
Keep the change small and well-tested.

options.name: material-aware-refuse
pros: Allows legitimate re-quorum after material change
cons: Slightly more logic than a blanket check

options.name: blanket-refuse-any-existing-runId
cons: False-blocks a legitimate re-quorum after a real material change and re-review

options.name: idempotent-silent-skip
cons: Hides double-submission; operator wanted an explicit refusal; inconsistent with existing REFUSAL style

rationale: Refusing only on the same (runId, materialDigest) blocks the real duplicate the operator flagged while not false-blocking a legitimate fresh quorum after a material change; an explicit refusal (vs silent skip) surfaces the mistake consistent with the existing REFUSAL constant.

preMortem.trigger: Guard keys on runId only, ignoring materialDigest
preMortem.consequence: After a real material change the operator cannot re-submit
preMortem.mitigation: Key the guard on (runId, materialDigest) so a new material does not collide

preMortem.trigger: rounds-knob case re-submits overlapping runIds at same material
preMortem.consequence: Suite goes red or, worse, is loosened to hide the guard
preMortem.mitigation: Restructure that case (fresh story / material change) and add explicit refuse + allow cases

preMortem.trigger: Reading verdicts from a different root than submitLocalVerdict writes
preMortem.consequence: Guard never fires or always fires
preMortem.mitigation: Read via listVerdicts(ctx.root,'local',storyId) — the same root submitLocalVerdict writes to
